generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Accounts of the family by Michigan State's and Hamburg's Botany Online, FloraBase and Plants of the World Online, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): minute unisexual flowers in cymose clusters; mostly 4 or 5 undifferentiated tepals, sometimes none; stamens as many as and opposite the tepals, their filaments inflexed in bud and springing out to shed pollen; ovary superior, 1-locular with one basal ovule, ostensibly of one carpel.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 71 Urticaceae: herbs, undershrubs or rarely soft-wooded trees, often with stinging hairs; leaves alternate or opposite, simple; stipules present, very rarely absent; flowers very small and of one sex; fruit a dry achene or a fleshy drupe.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Urticaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Cecropiaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 329, family Urticaceae: leaf arrangement alternate (spiral) or opposite; read as {"alternate": "often", "opposite": "often"}.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 329, family Urticaceae: leaf venation pinnate, palmate or unequally ternate; read as {"palmate": "often", "pinnate": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 329, family Urticaceae: inflorescence axillary cyme, globose head, spike or solitary; read as {"cyme": "often", "head": "often", "solitary": "often", "spike": "often"}.
